The move comes as disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz sharply reduce Iraq’s oil exports and put pressure on government revenues. Iraq’s crude exports have averaged about 1.25 million barrels a day since March, far below the nearly 3.5 million barrels a day recorded last year. France’s 10-year yield rose to 4.91%, versus 3.61% for the 2-year, steepening the curve to roughly 130bp. Lescure said demand for 10-year debt remains solid, but 30-year issuance is “a bit trickier” amid fiscal and political concerns.

text: Global Markets Rebound as Oil Prices Fall and AI Fears Ease US stock futures climbed as easing concerns over AI investments and falling oil prices lifted investor sentiment. S&P 500 futures gained 0.5%, while Nasdaq 100 futures advanced 0.9%, with chip stocks rebounding on renewed optimism surrounding OpenAI’s revenue outlook. Brent crude slipped below $103 a barrel amid hopes of reduced US-Iran tensions, while European stocks also recovered. Investors now turn their attention to upcoming corporate earnings, bond yields and geopolitical risks to determine whether the market rebound can sustain its momentum.

text: Deadly Attacks Hit Riyadh Airport, Three Killed Three Saudi Arabians were killed and others injured in two attacks targeting facilities at Riyadh’s King Khalid International Airport and a Saudia Airlines aircraft, according to Saudi authorities. The plane was reportedly hit while parked at the airport, with no passengers on board. The attacks come amid escalating Houthi strikes against Saudi Arabia, raising fresh concerns over regional security and aviation safety. Saudia said it resumed operations on Thursday evening as tensions across the Middle East continue to threaten travel and stability.

text: Australian Wheat Exports Set to Surge 47% Amid Black Sea Disruptions Australia is on track to export around 2.6 million tonnes of grain in October, 47% above the five-year average, as escalating attacks on Black Sea ships and grain terminals disrupt wheat supplies from Russia and Ukraine. Wheat is expected to account for roughly two-thirds of shipments, making this Australia's busiest October for grain exports in 16 years. Rising demand from the Philippines, Indonesia, China and other markets is boosting Australia's role in global grain trade. Meanwhile, wheat, soybean and corn futures edged higher, as traders monitor supply disruptions, export flows and geopolitical risks shaping agricultural commodity prices.
